```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation (both models): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_cyno"))$reference`
* Monkey model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_cyno"))$description`
* Human projection: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_human"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1080/19420862.2018.1465160>

Figueroa et al. (Genentech) built a two-compartment model with linear
non-specific clearance and a Michaelis-Menten (MM) target-mediated
elimination term for an anti-CD33 IgG1. Because receptor occupancy (RO) of
circulating CD33 reports how saturated the target sink is, RO was fitted
together with total-antibody (TAB) concentrations, using the same `KM`:

$$\frac{dC_1}{dt} = \frac{CL_D}{V_1}C_2 - \frac{CL_D}{V_1}C_1 - \frac{CL}{V_1}C_1 - \frac{V_{max}}{V_1(K_M + C_1)}C_1$$

$$\frac{dC_2}{dt} = -\frac{CL_D}{V_2}C_2 + \frac{CL_D}{V_2}C_1, \qquad RO(\%) = \frac{C_1}{K_M + C_1}\times 100$$

The model was fitted to the **unconjugated** antibody in monkeys (where higher
doses are tolerated), used without refitting to predict the TAB PK of the
pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) **ADC** in a monkey toxicology study, and then scaled
to humans. The paper therefore contributes two model files:

* `Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_cyno`: the monkey fit (Table 3, "Fitted Monkey").
* `Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_human`: the human projection (Table 3, "Predicted
  Human"), with `Vmax` at the 1-fold monkey value. The paper explores 3- and
  10-fold `Vmax`; the vignette sets these through `ini()`.

All parameters are per kg of body weight, so a dose in ug/kg gives a
concentration in ug/mL. Neither model has between-subject variability: the
monkey data were fitted with a naive-pooled approach.

# Population

The monkey fit used six healthy cynomolgus monkeys given a single IV bolus of
the unconjugated anti-CD33 mAb at 0.5 or 15 mg/kg (n = 3 each). Dosing-solution
assays found 64% and 86% of the nominal concentrations, so the fit used the
measured doses, 0.32 and 12.9 mg/kg. TAB was sampled from 15 minutes to 42 days
(LLOQ 7.8 ng/mL); CD33 RO on monocytes and granulocytes was sampled on days 1,
6, 21 and 42. ADA were detected in 5 of 6 animals without an apparent effect on
TAB. The separate ADC toxicology study dosed 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 and 1 mg/kg
(n = 4, 4, 1, 1; LLOQ 1 ug/mL). The human model is a projection for patients
with AML; no human data were used.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_cyno")()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Monkey | Human | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, mL/day/kg) | log(4.92) | fixed(log(4.92)) | Table 3, CL |
| `lq` (CLD, mL/day/kg) | log(22.7) | fixed(log(22.7)) | Table 3, CLD |
| `lvc` (V1, mL/kg) | log(36.7) | fixed(log(36.7)) | Table 3, V1 |
| `lvp` (V2, mL/kg) | log(18.1) | fixed(log(18.1)) | Table 3, V2 |
| `lvmax` (Vmax, ug/day/kg) | log(22.4) | fixed(log(22.4)); range 22.4 to 224 | Table 3, Vmax |
| `lkm` (KM, ug/mL) | log(10^-1.22) = log(0.0603) | fixed(log(10^-1.22)) | Table 3, alpha = log(KM) = -1.22; KM = 0.0602 |
| `propSd`, `addSd_RO` | fixed(0) | fixed(0) | Not reported (Materials and methods, 'PKPD modeling') |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | | | Equations 1 and 2 (in amounts) |
| `RO`, `RA` | | | Equation 3; RA = 100 - RO (Materials and methods) |

The paper fitted `log(KM)` and prints alpha = -1.22 next to KM = 0.0602 ug/mL
and CLINT = Vmax/KM = 372 mL/kg/day. Only base 10 reconciles these
(10^-1.22 = 0.0603; exp(-1.22) = 0.295), so `lkm` is the natural log of
10^-1.22.

```{r param-check}
mod_cyno <- readModelDb("Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_cyno")
ini_cyno <- rxode2::rxode(mod_cyno)$iniDf
pv <- setNames(ini_cyno$est, ini_cyno$name)
km <- exp(pv[["lkm"]])
clint <- exp(pv[["lvmax"]]) / km
stopifnot(
  abs(km - 0.0602) < 0.0005,       # Table 3, KM = 0.0602 ug/mL
  abs(clint - 372) < 2,            # Table 3, CLINT = 372 mL/kg/day
  abs(clint / exp(pv[["lcl"]]) - 75) < 1  # text: 'roughly 75-fold' CL
)
c(KM = km, CLINT = clint)
```

# Helpers

Both models are deterministic, so every simulation below is a typical-value
solve; no virtual cohort is needed. Each scenario is one `id`.

```{r helpers}
# One IV bolus at time 0 into the central compartment per scenario, plus
# observation rows at `times`. Scenario labels travel with `keep`. The models
# have two endpoints (Cc and RO), so observation rows carry `dvid = 1L`;
# every solve still returns Cc, RO and RA as columns.
bolus_events <- function(scen, times) {
  scen <- scen |> dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
  dose <- scen |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs <- scen |>
    dplyr::select(-amt) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

# Time at which `y` first crosses `level` (linear interpolation).
cross_time <- function(time, y, level) {
  i <- which(diff(sign(y - level)) != 0)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  time[i] + (level - y[i]) * (time[i + 1] - time[i]) / (y[i + 1] - y[i])
}

# The models have no etas, so rxode2's "multi-subject simulation without
# 'omega'" warning is expected here; only that warning is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
solve_det <- function(mod, ev, keep) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
      mod,
      events = ev, keep = keep, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
    )),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
}
```

# Monkey fit to the unconjugated antibody (Figure 3)

```{r fig3}
fine <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.01), seq(1, 50, by = 0.05))))
scen3 <- tibble::tibble(
  group = c("0.5 mg/kg", "15 mg/kg"),
  amt = c(0.64 * 500, 0.86 * 15000) # measured doses, ug/kg
)
sim3 <- solve_det(mod_cyno, bolus_events(scen3, fine), keep = "group")

# Concentrations decay into solver noise long after the target sink clears.
stopifnot(all(sim3$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim3$Cc)))

sim3 |>
  dplyr::filter(Cc > 0.1) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "TAB concentration (ug/mL)", colour = "Dose",
    title = "Figure 3a: anti-CD33 mAb in cynomolgus monkeys",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Figueroa 2018 (model curves; measured doses)."
  )

ggplot(sim3, aes(time, RA, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Receptor availability (%) = 100 - RO",
    colour = "Dose",
    title = "Figure 3b: CD33 receptor availability",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3b of Figueroa 2018."
  )
```

Figure 3 read-offs. The fitted curves reach the 0.1 ug/mL axis floor at about
day 9 (0.5 mg/kg) and day 45 (15 mg/kg), and receptor availability returns to
half at about day 9.5 and day 45. These are typical-value read-offs from the
published plot, so the bounds allow for the reading resolution of about one day.

```{r fig3-check}
fig3_cross <- sim3 |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    t_c01 = cross_time(time, Cc, 0.1),
    t_ra50 = cross_time(time, RA, 50),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(fig3_cross, digits = 2,
             caption = "Model crossing times (day).")
lo <- fig3_cross[fig3_cross$group == "0.5 mg/kg", ]
hi <- fig3_cross[fig3_cross$group == "15 mg/kg", ]
stopifnot(
  nrow(lo) == 1, nrow(hi) == 1,
  abs(lo$t_c01 - 9) < 1, abs(hi$t_c01 - 45) < 1.5,
  abs(lo$t_ra50 - 9.5) < 1, abs(hi$t_ra50 - 45) < 1.5
)
```

## PKNCA against Table 2

Table 2 summarises observed NCA. Its CL is the **nominal** dose divided by
AUCinf (15.5 x 32.5 = 504 and 8.63 x 1740 = 15016 ug/kg), while the model was
fitted to the measured doses. The comparison below therefore simulates the
measured doses on the study's sampling grid, treats values below the 7.8 ng/mL
LLOQ as missing (as the paper did), and divides the **nominal** dose by
AUCinf. Cmax is taken from the 15-minute first sample onward.

```{r pknca-cyno}
study_times <- c(0, 15 / 1440, 4 / 24, 12 / 24, 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42)
sim_nca_raw <- solve_det(mod_cyno, bolus_events(scen3, study_times),
                         keep = "group")
sim_nca <- sim_nca_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0 | Cc >= 0.0078) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group)
stopifnot(all(sim_nca$Cc > 0))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_df <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:2, time = 0, group = scen3$group,
  amt = c(500, 15000) # nominal, matching Table 2's CL = Dose / AUCinf
)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id,
                             route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 15 / 1440), end = Inf,
  aucinf.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE), half.life = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cl.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE), cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_cyno <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                           intervals = intervals))

published_t2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,      ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life, ~cl.obs,
  "0.5 mg/kg", 11.5,  32.5,        2.20,       15.5,
  "15 mg/kg",  272,   1740,        5.69,       8.63
)
cmp_t2 <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_cyno,
  reference = published_t2,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "day*ug/mL", half.life = "day",
            cl.obs = "mL/day/kg"),
  tolerance_pct = 20,
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
)
knitr::kable(cmp_t2, caption = paste(
  "Model (typical value, measured dose, study sampling) vs. observed NCA",
  "(Table 2). * differs from the reference by more than 20%."
))
```

The terminal half-lives agree with Table 2 within about 10%. Cmax, AUCinf and
CL differ by 22% to 39%, and this is a property of the published fit, not of
the transcription. (PKNCA labels the dose / AUCinf row `CL/F`; for this IV
bolus it is CL.) The naive-pooled fit with proportional weighting
does not pass through the group means: Figure 3a shows the 15 mg/kg curve above
the observed means on days 7 to 14, which is where most of the AUC lies, and the
0.5 mg/kg curve below the early observations. The model reproduces the plotted
curves (previous section), so the table is reported for context. The gate below
checks only the internal consistency of the comparison: the model's CL is the
nominal dose over the model's own AUCinf, and the high-dose AUC exceeds the
low-dose AUC by more than the dose ratio, as non-linear PK requires.

```{r pknca-cyno-check}
res <- as.data.frame(nca_cyno)
auc <- res$PPORRES[res$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]
names(auc) <- res$group[res$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]
cl <- res$PPORRES[res$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs"]
names(cl) <- res$group[res$PPTESTCD == "cl.obs"]
stopifnot(
  length(auc) == 2, length(cl) == 2,
  abs(cl[["0.5 mg/kg"]] * auc[["0.5 mg/kg"]] / 500 - 1) < 1e-6,
  auc[["15 mg/kg"]] / auc[["0.5 mg/kg"]] > (0.86 * 15000) / (0.64 * 500)
)
```

The PK-only fits of Table S1 (KM fixed at 1, 10 or 100 times KD) were reported
to show that Vmax is not identifiable without RO data. They are sensitivity
analyses rather than the final model and are not packaged.

# Monkey prediction of the ADC toxicology study (Figure 4)

```{r fig4}
scen4 <- tibble::tibble(
  group = c("0.1 mg/kg", "0.2 mg/kg", "0.4 mg/kg", "1 mg/kg"),
  amt = c(100, 200, 400, 1000)
)
grid4 <- seq(0, 16, by = 0.01)
sim4 <- solve_det(mod_cyno, bolus_events(scen4, grid4), keep = "group")
stopifnot(all(sim4$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim4$Cc)))

sim4 |>
  dplyr::filter(Cc > 0.3, time <= 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "TAB concentration (ug/mL)", colour = "ADC dose",
    title = "Figure 4a: predicted ADC TAB (LLOQ dotted)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4a of Figueroa 2018."
  )

sim4 |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, RA, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Receptor availability (%)", colour = "ADC dose",
    title = "Figure 4b: predicted receptor availability",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4b of Figueroa 2018."
  )
```

The Results state that the two lowest doses fall below the 1 ug/mL LLOQ
before day 7, that 0.4 and 1 mg/kg stay above it for about one and two weeks,
and that 1 mg/kg keeps RO above 90% for more than 15 days. Figure 4 places the
LLOQ crossings near days 1.5, 4.2, 8.3 and just after 15, and the 50%
availability crossings near days 3.8, 6.7 and 10.8.

```{r fig4-check}
fig4 <- sim4 |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    t_lloq = cross_time(time, Cc, 1),
    t_ra50 = cross_time(time, RA, 50),
    ro_cmax = max(RO),
    ro_day15 = RO[which.min(abs(time - 15))],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(fig4, digits = 2,
             caption = "Model LLOQ and 50%-availability crossings (day) and RO (%).")
g <- function(nm, col) {
  v <- fig4[[col]][fig4$group == nm]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row for ", nm)
  v
}
stopifnot(
  g("0.1 mg/kg", "t_lloq") < 7, g("0.2 mg/kg", "t_lloq") < 7,
  abs(g("0.1 mg/kg", "t_lloq") - 1.5) < 0.5,
  abs(g("0.2 mg/kg", "t_lloq") - 4.2) < 0.5,
  abs(g("0.4 mg/kg", "t_lloq") - 8.3) < 0.7,
  g("1 mg/kg", "t_lloq") > 15,
  abs(g("0.1 mg/kg", "t_ra50") - 3.8) < 0.5,
  abs(g("0.2 mg/kg", "t_ra50") - 6.7) < 0.5,
  abs(g("0.4 mg/kg", "t_ra50") - 10.8) < 0.7,
  g("1 mg/kg", "ro_day15") > 90
)
```

Two notes on Figure 4. In panel (b) the legend colours of 0.1 and 0.2 mg/kg are
swapped relative to panel (a): the curve labelled 0.2 mg/kg recovers first, which
only the lower dose can do. And the text says 0.1 mg/kg reaches "almost 90%" RO
at Cmax, whereas Equation 3 at Cmax = 100/36.7 = 2.72 ug/mL gives
`r round(g("0.1 mg/kg", "ro_cmax"), 1)`%, consistent with the Figure 4b curve
starting near zero availability.

# Human projection (Table 4 and Figure S1)

```{r human-setup}
mod_hum <- readModelDb("Figueroa_2018_antiCD33ADC_human")
vmax_fold <- function(mod, fold) {
  v <- log(22.4 * fold)
  rxode2::ini(mod, lvmax = v)
}
mods_hum <- list(
  "1x Vmax" = mod_hum,
  "3x Vmax" = vmax_fold(mod_hum, 3),
  "10x Vmax" = vmax_fold(mod_hum, 10)
)
```

```{r human-sim}
grid_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.002), seq(1, 6, by = 0.01))))
scen_h <- tibble::tibble(
  dose = c("0.25 ug/kg", "2.4 ug/kg", "21 ug/kg"),
  amt = c(0.25, 2.4, 21)
)
sim_h <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods_hum), function(nm) {
  solve_det(mods_hum[[nm]], bolus_events(scen_h, grid_h), keep = "dose") |>
    dplyr::mutate(vmax = nm)
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(vmax = factor(vmax, levels = names(mods_hum)))
stopifnot(all(sim_h$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_h$Cc)))

sim_h |>
  dplyr::filter(Cc > 1e-4) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, 1000 * Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~vmax) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "TAB concentration (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose",
    title = "Figure S1 (a, c, e): projected human PK",
    caption = "Replicates the central curves of Figure S1 of Figueroa 2018."
  )

ggplot(sim_h, aes(time, RA, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~vmax) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Receptor availability (%)", colour = "Dose",
    title = "Figure S1 (b, d, f): projected receptor availability",
    caption = "Replicates the central curves of Figure S1 of Figueroa 2018."
  )
```

Table 4 reports Cmax, RO at Cmax and AUC0-t, where t is 120, 72 and 24 h for
1-, 3- and 10-fold `Vmax`. AUC0-t is computed with PKNCA per dose and `Vmax`
scenario.

```{r pknca-human}
tend <- c("1x Vmax" = 5, "3x Vmax" = 3, "10x Vmax" = 1)
h_nca <- sim_h |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    scenario = paste(vmax, dose, sep = " | "),
    Cc_ng = pmax(1000 * Cc, 0)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc_ng)] |
                  Cc_ng >= 1e-6 * max(Cc_ng)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, vmax, dose, id, time, Cc_ng)
h_dose <- h_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(scenario, vmax, dose, id) |>
  dplyr::left_join(scen_h, by = "dose") |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0)
conc_h <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(h_nca, Cc_ng ~ time | scenario + id)
dose_h <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(h_dose, amt ~ time | scenario + id,
                           route = "intravascular")
int_h <- h_dose |>
  dplyr::distinct(scenario, vmax) |>
  dplyr::mutate(start = 0, end = tend[as.character(vmax)],
                auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, start, end, auclast, cmax) |>
  as.data.frame()
nca_h <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_h, dose_h, intervals = int_h)
))

table4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~vmax,      ~dose,        ~auc_pub, ~auc_p05, ~auc_p95, ~cmax_pub, ~ro_pub,
  "1x Vmax",  "0.25 ug/kg", 0.515,    0.214,    2.63,     6.81,      10,
  "3x Vmax",  "0.25 ug/kg", 0.175,    0.0611,   1.52,     6.81,      10,
  "10x Vmax", "0.25 ug/kg", 0.052,    0.0169,   0.458,    6.81,      10,
  "1x Vmax",  "2.4 ug/kg",  8.37,     4.49,     32.4,     65.4,      52,
  "3x Vmax",  "2.4 ug/kg",  2.88,     1.31,     18.7,     65.4,      52,
  "10x Vmax", "2.4 ug/kg",  0.871,    0.389,    5.80,     65.4,      52,
  "1x Vmax",  "21 ug/kg",   236,      158,      544,      572,       90,
  "3x Vmax",  "21 ug/kg",   90.4,     52.9,     322,      572,       90,
  "10x Vmax", "21 ug/kg",   29.1,     16.7,     110,      572,       90
)
ro_cmax <- sim_h |>
  dplyr::group_by(vmax, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ro_sim = max(RO), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(vmax = as.character(vmax))
t4 <- nca_h |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::separate(scenario, c("vmax", "dose"), sep = " \\| ") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table4, by = c("vmax", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(ro_cmax, by = c("vmax", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_ratio = auc_pub / auclast)
stopifnot(nrow(t4) == 9)
t4 |>
  dplyr::select(vmax, dose, cmax, cmax_pub, ro_sim, ro_pub,
                auclast, auc_pub, auc_p05, auc_p95, auc_ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Vmax" = vmax, "Dose" = dose,
    "Cmax sim (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Cmax Table 4" = cmax_pub,
    "RO at Cmax sim (%)" = ro_sim, "RO at Cmax Table 4" = ro_pub,
    "AUC0-t sim (ng*day/mL)" = auclast, "AUC0-t Table 4" = auc_pub,
    "Table 4 5th pct" = auc_p05, "Table 4 95th pct" = auc_p95,
    "Table 4 / sim" = auc_ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Projected human exposure vs. Table 4.")
```

Cmax and RO at Cmax match Table 4 to its printed precision; both are set by
`V1` and `KM` alone. The AUC0-t values printed in Table 4 are 5% to 26% below
the typical-value solve at the Table 3 estimates, by a ratio that depends on
dose (about 0.74, 0.88 and 0.94 at 0.25, 2.4 and 21 ug/kg) but hardly on
the `Vmax` fold. The paper does not print the Vmax-log(KM) covariance it
sampled from, so the source of the offset cannot be traced. A `KM` near
0.044 ug/mL reproduces the low- and high-dose rows but not the middle one,
so it is not a simple `KM` rounding. The packaged model keeps the printed
estimates. Every typical-value AUC lies inside the paper's 5th to 95th
percentile range, and the gate checks that and the exact Cmax and RO values.

```{r human-check}
stopifnot(
  all(abs(t4$cmax / t4$cmax_pub - 1) < 0.005),
  all(abs(t4$ro_sim - t4$ro_pub) < 1),
  all(t4$auclast > t4$auc_p05 & t4$auclast < t4$auc_p95),
  all(t4$auc_ratio > 0.65 & t4$auc_ratio < 1)
)
```

# Comparison with clinical anti-CD33 molecules (Figure 5)

## Lintuzumab receptor availability on day 7 (Figure 5a)

Lintuzumab binds CD33 with about 20-fold lower affinity, so the paper set
`KM` to 20 times the anti-CD33 ADC value (about 1.2 ug/mL) and kept the
human `Vmax` range.

```{r fig5a}
doses5 <- 10^seq(2, 4, by = 0.05)
scen5 <- tibble::tibble(dose = doses5, amt = doses5)
sim5a <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods_hum), function(nm) {
  m <- rxode2::ini(mods_hum[[nm]], lkm = log(20 * 10^-1.22))
  solve_det(m, bolus_events(scen5, 7), keep = "dose") |>
    dplyr::mutate(vmax = nm)
})) |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 7) |>
  dplyr::mutate(vmax = factor(vmax, levels = names(mods_hum)))

ggplot(sim5a, aes(dose, RA, linetype = vmax)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (ug/kg)", y = "Receptor availability on day 7 (%)",
    linetype = "Human Vmax",
    title = "Figure 5a: lintuzumab (KM x 20)",
    caption = "Replicates the model curves of Figure 5a of Figueroa 2018."
  )

ra50 <- sim5a |>
  dplyr::group_by(vmax) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dose_ra50 = 10^cross_time(log10(dose), RA, 50),
                   ra_100 = RA[which.min(abs(dose - 100))],
                   .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(ra50, digits = 1,
             caption = "Dose giving 50% availability on day 7, and availability at 100 ug/kg.")
```

Figure 5a read-offs: the 1-fold curve starts near 80% at 100 ug/kg, and the
three curves pass 50% near 250-300, 600-700 and 2000 ug/kg.

```{r fig5a-check}
r <- function(nm, col) {
  v <- ra50[[col]][as.character(ra50$vmax) == nm]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row for ", nm)
  v
}
stopifnot(
  abs(r("1x Vmax", "ra_100") - 80) < 8,
  r("1x Vmax", "dose_ra50") > 220, r("1x Vmax", "dose_ra50") < 350,
  r("3x Vmax", "dose_ra50") > 550, r("3x Vmax", "dose_ra50") < 800,
  r("10x Vmax", "dose_ra50") > 1700, r("10x Vmax", "dose_ra50") < 2400
)
```

## Clearance as a function of dose (Figure 5b)

The paper compares GO and AVE9633 clearances with the model's dose / AUC over
100 to 10000 ug/kg.

```{r fig5b}
doses5b <- c(100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000)
grid5b <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.005), seq(2, 20, by = 0.02),
                        seq(20, 90, by = 0.1))))
scen5b <- tibble::tibble(dose = doses5b, amt = doses5b)
sim5b <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods_hum), function(nm) {
  solve_det(mods_hum[[nm]], bolus_events(scen5b, grid5b), keep = "dose") |>
    dplyr::mutate(vmax = nm)
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = paste(vmax, dose, sep = " | "))
stopifnot(all(sim5b$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim5b$Cc)))

conc5b <- sim5b |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario) |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-9 * max(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, id, time, Cc)
dose5b <- sim5b |>
  dplyr::distinct(scenario, vmax, dose, id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose)
nca5b <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc5b, Cc ~ time | scenario + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose5b, amt ~ time | scenario + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cl.last = TRUE)
))) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cl.last") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(dose5b, scenario, vmax, dose),
                   by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::mutate(vmax = factor(vmax, levels = names(mods_hum)))

ggplot(nca5b, aes(dose, PPORRES, linetype = vmax)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (ug/kg)", y = "CL = dose / AUC (mL/day/kg)",
    linetype = "Human Vmax",
    title = "Figure 5b: projected clearance versus dose",
    caption = "Replicates the model curves of Figure 5b of Figueroa 2018."
  )
cl_tab <- nca5b |>
  dplyr::arrange(vmax, dose) |>
  dplyr::select(vmax, dose, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = vmax, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dose)
knitr::kable(cl_tab, digits = 1, caption = "Projected CL (mL/day/kg).")
```

Figure 5b read-offs: the 1-fold curve falls from about 30 mL/day/kg at
100 ug/kg to about 8 at 1000 and 5.5 at 10000; the 3-fold curve starts near
65 at 100 ug/kg; all three meet near 5 to 9 at 10000 ug/kg, approaching the
non-specific CL of 4.92.

```{r fig5b-check}
clv <- function(nm, d) {
  v <- nca5b$PPORRES[as.character(nca5b$vmax) == nm & nca5b$dose == d]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row for ", nm, " ", d)
  v
}
stopifnot(
  abs(clv("1x Vmax", 100) / 30 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(clv("1x Vmax", 1000) / 8 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(clv("1x Vmax", 10000) / 5.5 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(clv("3x Vmax", 100) / 65 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(clv("10x Vmax", 10000) / 9 - 1) < 0.15,
  all(nca5b$PPORRES > 4.92)
)
```

The 10-fold curve in the published Figure 5b sits about tenfold above this
solve at the low-dose end (about 1800 versus
`r round(clv("10x Vmax", 100))` mL/day/kg at 100 ug/kg) while agreeing at
10000 ug/kg. No single `Vmax` multiple reproduces the published 10-fold curve
over the whole range (a 100-fold `Vmax` gives about 1600 at 100 ug/kg but 31
at 10000), and the 1- and 3-fold curves and the Figure 5a curves match, so the
packaged model is left as printed and the 10-fold low-dose end is not gated.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Log base of `KM`.** Table 3 prints alpha = log(KM) = -1.22 together with
  KM = 0.0602 ug/mL and CLINT = 372 mL/kg/day. Only base 10 reconciles these,
  so `lkm = log(10^-1.22)`.
- **Per-kg parameterisation.** The paper reports every parameter per kg and
  scales monkey to human with a body-weight exponent of 1, so the models use
  ug/kg doses and mL/kg volumes rather than a body-weight covariate.
- **Measured doses for the monkey fit.** The fit used the measured doses (64% and
  86% of nominal: 0.32 and 12.9 mg/kg). Table 2's CL uses nominal doses, which is
  reproduced in the PKNCA comparison.
- **Residual error.** The paper used proportional weighting for PK and constant
  weighting for RO but reports no magnitudes, so `propSd` and `addSd_RO` are
  `fixed(0)`.
- **No between-subject variability.** The fit was naive-pooled.
- **Human `Vmax`.** Table 3 gives a 22.4 to 224 ug/day/kg range. The packaged
  human model uses the 1-fold value; the 3- and 10-fold scenarios are set
  through `ini()` above.
- **Parameter uncertainty.** The paper's 5th-95th percentile bands come from
  1000 draws of (Vmax, log KM) from the estimates' covariance matrix, which is
  not printed (only the SEs are), so the bands are quoted, not re-simulated.
- **Table 4 AUC0-t.** The printed values are 5% to 26% below the typical-value
  solve at the printed estimates; they are within the paper's own percentile
  bands. See the human projection section.
- **Figure 5b, 10-fold curve.** It does not match a 10-fold `Vmax` at low doses;
  see the Figure 5 section.
- **Figure 4b legend** swaps the 0.1 and 0.2 mg/kg colours, and the text's
  "almost 90%" RO at Cmax for 0.1 mg/kg is about 98% by Equation 3.
- **Unconjugated antibody vs. ADC.** The monkey model was fitted to the
  unconjugated antibody and applied to the ADC on the paper's assumption that
  conjugation at LC K149C changes neither non-specific clearance nor target
  binding; both models describe total antibody.
- No correction notice for the article was found in Europe PMC (checked
  2026-11-25).
